tx_southeast_face.blurb: The largest of the climbing zones on Buzzard's Roost, out at Enchanted Rock in the Texas Hill Country. Seventeen granite lines, mostly trad with a handful of bolted sport routes, run from about 5.7 up to the 5.12 range, with the bulk sitting between 5.9 and 5.11. Two opposing walls meet in a big corner, and a few routes begin inside caves made by fallen boulders, which makes those a reasonable pick when summer heat is a problem. The face tends to be shaded in the afternoon. Reaching Buzzard's Roost takes the longest walk of any zone in the park, so it is a good fallback on days when the busier areas are packed.

tx_sneed_s_cory.blurb: A compact crag in the Tom Mays Unit of Franklin Mountains State Park, on the west side of El Paso. Most of the seventeen routes are sport, with a few trad lines and one short boulder problem, and the climbing spans easy 5.6 terrain up to 5.12. Plenty of the grades fall between 5.8 and 5.11, so it suits a mixed group. Walls are short and featured, with fun moves rather than long pitches. The face stays in shade until late morning, and the short walk from the lot makes it handy for an afternoon session, though weekends can bring a crowd.

tx_holladay_wall.blurb: A shady limestone wall on the North Shore side of Reimers Ranch near Austin, a short stroll beyond the Awesome Roof ledge. Nearly all of its sixteen routes are bolted sport lines, plus one trad route. Grades start around 5.9, cluster heavily in the 5.10s, and thin out through 5.11 and 5.12 to a single 5.13. Several routes begin from single-bolt starts off a carpeted ledge. It rarely gets crowded. Be aware that North Shore rock can be friable and the ledges muddy, so check holds before trusting them.

tx_cheech_and_chong_wall.blurb: A limestone sport wall on the North Shore side of Reimers Ranch, west of Austin. It looks a bit scruffy from a distance but holds a good number of quality lines: fifteen bolted routes and one top rope. Grades run from roughly 5.8 to 5.12, with most climbs in the 5.10 to 5.11 range, so it works best for intermediate climbers. It is reached by following the main trail across the stream and branching off toward Gypsy Wall. Watch for loose rock and muddy ledges, which are common on this part of the park.

tx_philosophy_wall.blurb: A limestone top-rope wall tucked into the North Shore side of Reimers Ranch near Austin, and one of the least visited spots there. Twelve of the sixteen routes are top ropes, with a couple of sport lines and two trad routes. Grades run from 5.6 to 5.10, making it one of the friendlier places for newer climbers or anyone setting up laps. Many lines share bolted anchors at the top, and some need long slings rather than quickdraws. Walk down, cross the creek, and bushwhack up to the base, watching for poison ivy on the way.

tx_bad_boulder_the.blurb: A single steep limestone boulder on the south side of Barton Creek in the Greenbelt, grouped with the Hill of Life bouldering. Sixteen problems range from V0 to V8, with most in the V0 to V6 band and a couple of hard ones at the top end. The style is thin pockets, long reaches and tricky top-outs, so expect finger strength over power. Reaching it means a hike of around twenty-five minutes, including a creek crossing that is easy to miss. Bring several pads and a spotter, since the landings are uneven.

tx_sex_cave.blurb: A steep cave at the mouth of the canyon into Reimers Ranch near Austin, and the first crag you reach walking in along the creek. Fourteen sport routes and two boulder problems climb short, powerful lines on limestone, using big tufas and pockets. The sport grades start at 5.11 and sit mostly in the 5.12s and 5.13s, so this is a wall for strong, experienced climbers rather than beginners. Because the cave is overhanging, routes tend to be short but sustained.
